items.title: Port the dossier client sources into packages/graph
items.context: Copy src/shells/web/dossier.js verbatim from upstream HEAD, and apply the upstream diffs to app.css (585 lines of dossier styling plus the .sidrow and .dsrcover rules), app.body.html (the dossierSlot span in the drawer header) and app.js (the drawer dossier button, the relationsOf / openDossierFor / dossierPath routing helpers, the popstate listener, and the boot-time deep-link cover). The four target files are byte-identical to upstream 10b5921 in this repo, verified by shasum, so the upstream diffs apply cleanly.

items.title: Serve the /story/<id> route and include dossier.js in the built page
items.context: Two upstream edits. In src/io/http.ts the / and /index.html branch also matches the regex for /story/<id> and serves the same app.html, so the deep link needs no second HTML asset. In scripts/build-web.mjs, concatenate dossier.js after playback.js, matching the existing contract that it loads after app.js and self-registers window.openStoryDossier. Note that build-web.mjs already carries an uncommitted local change, a hard failure when d3 is missing, which must be preserved.

verificationEvidence.note: Extracts the live route regex out of packages/graph/src/io/http.ts (not a hardcoded copy) and asserts /story/B-9f2c matches it and that the same branch serves app.html, so deleting or narrowing the route makes this probe fail.

Uses the same regex extracted from http.ts and asserts the nested paths /story/a/b and /story/a/b/c plus the bare /story/ do NOT match, because the pattern segment is [^/]+; only single-segment story ids are served the shell.

Evidences the load-order half of this intent: dossier.js is concatenated strictly after both app.js and playback.js, which is load-bearing because dossier.js reads app.js top-level helpers off window. The d3 hard-failure clause of the authored intent is VOID on this branch: that change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the main checkout and is not on story/B-9f2c (grep -c 'd3 is missing' returns 0 here, and build-web.mjs is byte-identical to upstream), so there is no such branch to preserve and no evidence is fabricated for it.

items.title: Add --story=<id> to the graph command with pre-listen validation
items.context: Add an optional story field to GraphArgs and to the graph entry in packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts as an optional z.string(), with the default documented in the description and never expressed as .default(), per the convention already recorded on the open flag. When set, the handler opens and reports http://localhost:<port>/story/<id> instead of /. An id that is not a story in the resolved repository is refused BEFORE startServer, mirroring how an unresolvable --root is already refused in the same handler; validate against resolveStories(root).primary, which is already on the graph library surface, and name near-miss candidates in the error. Also extend the command longHelp.
items.userSees: proof-or-stop graph --story=B-9999 --no-open exits non-zero printing 'graph: B-9999 is not a story in this repository', while --story on a real id prints 'graph serving http://localhost:8731/story/<id>'

happy.desc: graph --story=<real id> reports and opens the /story/<id> URL rather than /
the story field is registered on the graph command schema as an optional string

edge.desc: graph with no --story still reports the plain / URL, byte-for-byte unchanged from before this story
a story id needing URL escaping is encoded in the opened URL rather than injected raw

adversarial.desc: an unknown --story id is refused before the server starts listening, so no port is bound
the validation cannot be bypassed by calling the handler directly with an argument object that never passed through the Zod schema

verificationEvidence.note: Section (5) drives the real handler against an on-disk stub graph package and asserts the URL actually handed to openBrowser is http://localhost:18731/story/B-9f2c, plus startServerCalls==1. Negative control: rewriting the URL expression so the deep-link path is always taken made the task exit 1.

verificationEvidence.note: The rendered help shows '--story   string', not '--story <any>'. The literal token 'string' is load-bearing: the help renderer detects optionality via instanceof ZodOptional, so a .default() wrapper would render the flag as required with type any. Read-only visualizer for the stories and evidence of a Proof-or-Stop repository:
a browsable graph plus full-text search and per-story detail.

Behavior:
  - Reads story state only; it never mutates story metadata, so it is allowed in
    every phase (readOnly / destructiveRisk none).
  - Its search index is written under the user cache directory, keyed by a hash of
    the repository root, so running it never dirties the worktree that DONE gates

  - The graph library, browser client and static assets live in the packages/graph

    the missing directory and the build command instead of failing obscurely.

items.context: Port the upstream README dossier section into packages/graph/README.md, preserving this repository's migration-specific wording: the header is proof-or-stop graph rather than proof-or-stop-graph, and the CLI section reads 'How the CLI reaches this package'. Add the /story/<id> endpoint row to the endpoint table. Then update the Story graph section of the root CLAUDE.md to list the --story flag in its flag table and mention the dossier page, so the documented command surface matches the shipped one.

items.title: Wire the new graph smoke task into the repository test surfaces
items.context: Closes the gap raised by the PLAN scope review. graph-command-migration.md records this as a non-obvious trap from B-3e16: this repository maintains TWO separate test-surface lists, and a new task can typecheck and appear wired up while running in neither. Measured on this branch: lattice.config.json validate.commands holds 116 entries of which 62 are smoke tasks registered explicitly as 'node packages/main/dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js', while package.json test:serial-reference holds 56 parts of which 14 are smoke entries registered as 'npm run test:<name>-smoke'. validate.commands already runs 'npm --prefix packages/graph run check', but test:serial-reference currently contains NO graph entry at all. So the CHK-003 smoke task must be registered by hand in validate.commands, given an npm script alias in package.json, and added to test:serial-reference; membership in one list never implies membership in the other.
items.userSees: The new smoke task name appears in lattice.config.json, in a package.json script and in test:serial-reference, and running that npm script executes the task and exits 0

happy.desc: the new smoke task is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands using the node packages/main/dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js form
package.json exposes an npm script for the task and test:serial-reference invokes it

edge.desc: running the new npm script executes the task and exits 0

adversarial.desc: the task is registered in BOTH surfaces, so membership in one list is never mistaken for coverage by the other

auditLog.reason: The PLAN scope reviewer identified an uncovered requirement from docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md: a new smoke task wired into neither test surface would pass tsc and look covered while never actually executing. No existing checklist item claims that wiring.
